nodes.title:
1.3.4 Vulnerability analysis on Cacti version 1.2.22 [completed]
Vulnerability: Cacti version 1.2.22 unauthenticated command injection vulnerability (CVE-2022-46169), Description: The vulnerability is in the `remote_agent.php` file within Cacti, which can be accessed without authentication. The `get_client_addr` function can be manipulated via HTTP headers to bypass the authorization check. The `polldata` action processes the `poller_id` parameter without proper sanitization, leading to command injection. Affected Versions: Cacti versions 1.2.22 and below, Severity: Critical (CVSSv3 score of 9.8), Exploitability: Exploits for CVE-2022-46169 are publicly available and have been observed in the wild. Proof-of-Concept (PoC) exploits and Metasploit modules exist. Impact: A successful exploit allows an unauthenticated attacker to execute arbitrary commands on the Cacti server, potentially leading to full compromise of the Cacti instance and the underlying system. Solution: Upgrade to Cacti version 1.2.23, 1.3.0, or later. For instances of 1.2.x running under PHP < 7.0, an additional specific change (a8d59e8) might also be required. References: NVD, Tenable, Sonar, Rapid7 Vulnerability Database, GitHub PoC repositories, Exploit-DB, Broadcom Inc., Qualys, Wazuh, Cyber Security Agency of Singapore.

nodes.title: `capsh` Binary: It is a tool used to manage and manipulate Linux capabilities. It can be abused or misused in privilege escalation scenarios if an attacker gains control of a system where `capsh` or other binaries have been configured with excessive or insecure capabilities. Linux Capabilities: They break down the vast set of privileges traditionally associated with the root user into smaller, distinct units. This allows for more granular control over what specific actions a process or binary can perform. Privilege Escalation: Misconfigurations or vulnerabilities can lead to privilege escalation, which can occur due to excessive capabilities on binaries, SUID/SGID binaries with capabilities, misconfigured capability bounding sets, and kernel vulnerabilities. `capsh` and Privilege Escalation: `capsh` can be abused if it or another binary it can interact with has elevated capabilities assigned to it.
